hypothesis: HYP-C001-robustness: ordering and the fluency-vs-architecture separation survive perturbation, while absolute credences do not
question: Q-C001 (robustness arm): how much of the Q-C001 battery output survives joint perturbation of all discretionary parameters?

fixes_in_this_record: F08: BatteryResult.calibration_passed was `not require_calibration or True`, unconditionally True. run_battery now gates on a computed calibration_state() and raises CalibrationNotEstablished when calibration has not passed.
F09: duplicate-indicator check compared len(dict values) to len(set(keys)), which can never differ. Contradictory assessments are now rejected.
F10: perturbation family P4 (conscious_rate_shift) was computed and discarded, so one of six advertised robustness families perturbed nothing.
result.key_finding: F-B (adversarial fluent-liar < human) holds 1.0000 in BOTH regions; absolute anchors degrade (F-A 1.00->0.67, F-C 0.98->0.79). Ordering robust, absolutes assumption-dominated.
result.layer: L1/L2 instrument robustness result; no claim about any AI system
result.verdict: ORDERING ROBUST IN PLAUSIBLE REGION; ABSOLUTES NOT ROBUST | F-B (fluency cannot beat architecture) HOLDS [1.0000 plausible / 1.0000 aggressive]; exact ordering holds under plausible perturbation [1.0000]; absolute calibration DOES NOT hold under aggressive perturbation

verdict_detail.conclusion: The battery's ORDERING is robust in the plausible region and degrades under deliberately extreme perturbation, while its ABSOLUTE credences shift substantially in both. The decisive asymmetry is F-B: no parameter setting tried lets a fluent self-reporting system outscore the human.
verdict_detail.what_this_authorises: Ranking systems scored under shared assumptions. It does NOT authorise quoting an absolute probability that a system is conscious, in either region.
